title: Java News Roundup: New OpenJDK JEPs, CDI 5.0, Spring, Open Liberty, RefactorFirst, ADK for Kotlin
gist: The week of September 7th, 2026 in Java: JEP 544 (ahead-of-time code compilation) and JEP 543 (structured concurrency, finalizing after seven preview rounds spanning JDK 21 to JDK 27) both reached Candidate status ahead of the September 15 JDK 27 release. Agentic AI is now embedded in the Java platform itself — Jakarta Agentic AI 1.0 hit M1 with Azul Payara as first implementation, Open Liberty promoted its MCP Server feature to GA, and Google shipped ADK for Kotlin 1.0.

themes.theme: OpenJDK: startup performance and concurrency finalize

insights.claim: JEP 544, Ahead-of-Time Code Compilation, was elevated from JEP Draft 8335368 to Candidate status, proposing that the HotSpot JVM start with optimized native code already available so applications reach and sustain peak performance faster.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: AOT in mainline HotSpot narrows GraalVM Native Image's startup advantage and strengthens Java's case for serverless and scale-to-zero workloads.
insights.locator: JEP 544, Ahead-of-Time Code Compilation

insights.claim: JEP 543, Structured Concurrency, reached Candidate status proposing finalization without change after seven rounds of preview spanning JDK 21 through JDK 27, plus two incubator rounds in JDK 19 and JDK 20.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Nine total preview/incubator cycles for one API is a concrete measure of OpenJDK's deliberate pace — useful when forecasting when any JDK feature becomes safe to build on.
insights.locator: JEP 543, Structured Concurrency, has been elevated

insights.claim: Structured concurrency simplifies concurrent programming by treating groups of related tasks running in different threads as a single unit of work, streamlining error handling and cancellation while improving reliability and observability.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Finalization removes the last blocker to virtual-thread-based server architectures in conservative enterprises — a slow-burn driver of Java modernization spend.
insights.quote: treat groups of related tasks running in different threads as a single unit of work, thereby streamlining error handling and cancellation, improving reliability, and enhancing observability.
insights.locator: This feature simplifies concurrent programming

insights.claim: JDK 27 was scheduled for release on Tuesday, September 15, 2026, with JDK 28 already at early-access Build 15.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: A new Java LTS-cycle release landing sets the clock on enterprise migration budgets and vendor support-window changes.
insights.locator: JDK 27 will be released on Tuesday, September 15, 2026.

themes.theme: Agentic AI standardized into the Java platform

insights.claim: The Jakarta Agentic AI 1.0 specification, whose creation was approved in early November 2025, delivered an M1 release and a new project website, with the August 2026 edition of Azul Payara serving as the first implementation.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Enterprise Java is formalizing agentic AI as a standard rather than a library choice — a signal that agent infrastructure is entering regulated, long-lived enterprise stacks.
insights.locator: The Jakarta Agentic AI 1.0 specification

insights.claim: Open Liberty 26.0.0.9 elevated its MCP Server feature from experimental to general availability, making Model Context Protocol serving a supported capability of a mainstream Java application server.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: MCP reaching GA inside enterprise app servers is stronger evidence of protocol durability than startup adoption — it implies multi-year support commitments.
insights.locator: elevation of the MCP Server feature (mcp-1.0)

insights.claim: The Open Liberty MCP promotion carries breaking changes: the feature name changed from mcpServer-1.0 to mcp-1.0 and the server.xml configuration element changed from <mcpServer> to <mcp>.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Breaking renames at GA indicate the MCP integration surface is still settling — early adopters carry rework cost.
insights.locator: This release brings breaking changes

insights.claim: Google released ADK for Kotlin 1.0, delivering full feature parity with ADK 1.0 Core to Kotlin, Java and Android developers through an idiomatic Kotlin API plus Android-first, on-device extensions for building agents on the JVM or on-device.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Google extending its agent development kit to on-device Android is a distribution play for edge agents — watch for agent workloads shifting off cloud inference.
insights.quote: full feature parity with ADK 1.0 Core to Kotlin, Java, and Android developers through an idiomatic Kotlin API, and adds Android-first, on-device extensions for building agents on the JVM or on-device.
insights.locator: Google has released version 1.0 of the ADK for Kotlin

insights.claim: ADK for Kotlin 1.0 adds a MultiAgentLoader class providing a fixed set of agents by name alongside the existing SingleAgentLoader, plus a fluent builder() method on AdkServerConfig for Java developers.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Multi-agent loading as a first-class API confirms the industry has moved past single-agent deployments as the default shape.
insights.locator: New features include: a new MultiAgentLoader class

insights.claim: Spring Tools 5.4.0 enables the Claude Code plugin to render a project's logical structure, putting AI coding-agent integration directly into mainstream Spring tooling.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: IDE-level coding-agent hooks shipping in default Spring tooling is a distribution win for agent vendors inside the largest enterprise Java framework.
insights.locator: enabling the Claude Code plugin to render a project's logical structure

insights.claim: Jakarta Contexts and Dependency Injection 5.0 was approved by the Specification Committee as the first specification targeting Jakarta EE 12, a milestone because CDI is one of the most central specifications in the Platform.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: CDI landing first sets the dependency order and effectively starts the clock on the Jakarta EE 12 release train.
insights.quote: Jakarta Contexts and Dependency Injection (CDI) 5.0 was approved by the Specification Committee this week as the first specification targeting Jakarta EE 12.
insights.locator: In his weekly Hashtag Jakarta EE blog

insights.claim: The Starter for Jakarta EE has been redesigned to align with the Jakarta EE website, with the Eclipse Foundation soliciting developer feedback on the new UI.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Onboarding UX investment signals Jakarta EE is competing for greenfield projects, not just maintaining legacy installations.
insights.locator: The design of the Starter for Jakarta EE has been refreshed

insights.claim: Micronaut Framework 5.1.5 and 5.1.4 resolve three CVEs and upgrade to Netty 4.2.18.Final, which itself addresses numerous CVEs.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Netty sits under most JVM networking stacks, so a single Netty CVE wave forces coordinated patch releases across many frameworks — a systemic supply-chain concentration risk.
insights.locator: The Micronaut Foundation has released versions 5.1.5 and 5.1.4

insights.claim: Open Liberty 26.0.0.9 resolves numerous CVEs and implements OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728), letting developers enable protected resource metadata with the OpenID Connect Client feature.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: RFC 9728 support is a prerequisite for standards-based authorization of MCP servers — the same release shipping both is not a coincidence.
insights.locator: an implementation of the OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata

insights.claim: TornadoVM 6.1.0, released approximately one week after version 6.0, cuts fixed per-operation host cost by skipping upload of the per-launch 24-byte kernel-argument stack frame when contents are identical and skipping stream synchronisation when nothing has been enqueued.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Per-operation overhead dominates GPU-offload economics for fine-grained kernels; these micro-optimizations widen the range of Java workloads worth accelerating.
insights.locator: Approximately one week after the release of version 6.0

insights.claim: Gradle 9.8.0 RC1 delivers a 45% performance improvement on Windows, plus support for the upcoming Java 27 release in the Gradle daemon and Java toolchains and a flag to reuse Maven mirror repository settings.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: A 45% Windows build speedup directly cuts CI compute spend for Windows-based enterprise pipelines — a measurable cost line, not just developer comfort.
insights.locator: The first release candidate of Gradle 9.8.0

insights.claim: Apache Groovy 6.0.0 RC1 introduces a @GroovyABI annotation that marks methods callable directly from bytecode as part of the Groovy Application Binary Interface, formalizing a stable binary contract for the language.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: An explicit ABI is what lets downstream tools depend on Groovy internals safely — a maturity step for a language often written off as legacy.
insights.locator: a new @GroovyABI annotation that marks methods

insights.claim: Groovy 6.0.0 RC1 hardens JsonSlurper with a maxNumberLength attribute that rejects number tokens above a set length by throwing a JsonException, and improves XmlNodePrinter for larger documents.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Bounded number parsing is a denial-of-service mitigation — parser hardening is quietly becoming standard practice across JVM ecosystem libraries.
insights.locator: an improved JsonSlurper class that adds a maxNumberLength attribute

insights.claim: RefactorFirst 0.10.0, from Jim Bethancourt of Improving, raises the minimum Java version to JDK 17 and adds Kotlin source file processing so mixed Java and Kotlin codebases are analysed as a single unified codebase.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Refactoring-prioritization tools treating Java and Kotlin as one codebase confirms polyglot JVM is now the default enterprise reality, not an exception.
insights.locator: Jim Bethancourt, principal software consultant at Improving

insights.claim: Spring Tools 5.4.0 adds a validation check and quick fix replacing combined @Controller and @ResponseBody annotations with @RestController, and adopts the Spring Modulith @ApplicationModuleListener annotation.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Tooling nudges toward Spring Modulith show Pivotal-lineage stewards pushing modular monolith patterns over microservices as the default enterprise architecture.
insights.locator: The release of Spring Tools 5.4.0 ships with bug fixes
